# `clipdata`: cut out boxes, plots, and height ranges {#sec-clipdata}

## What it does

`clipdata` writes the points that fall inside a rectangle, inside (or
outside) a set of polygons, or within a range of heights above ground.
Its most common use is cutting field plots out of a lidar acquisition so
their points can be summarized and matched to field measurements.

With a polygon shapefile and `/multifile`, one run writes a separate file
for every polygon, named from one of the shapefile's fields. With
`/ground`, `/minz` and `/maxz` are heights above the ground surface
rather than raw elevations.

## Example commands

The example runs four clips: a 100 x 100 ft box; the same box keeping
only points 2 to 200 ft above ground; one file per 30 ft radius plot; and
everything outside both plots.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/clipdata_commands.md >}}

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/output` | `out/clipdata/box.las` | The clipped point cloud. With `/multifile`, a folder that receives one file per polygon. |
| `/extent` | `1023780,598900,1023880,599000` | Keep points inside this rectangle, given as lower-left X, lower-left Y, upper-right X, upper-right Y. |
| `/ground` | `out/ground_dem.tif` | Ground surface; makes `/minz` and `/maxz` heights above ground. |
| `/minz`, `/maxz` | `2`, `200` | Keep points 2 to 200 ft above ground. |
| `/shape` | `out/clipdata/example_plots.shp` | Keep points inside the shapefile's polygons. Combined with `/extent`, both apply. |
| `/multifile` | | With `/shape`, write one file per polygon. A polygon with no points gets no file. |
| `/field` | `plot_id` | With `/multifile`, name each file from this attribute (`plotA.laz`, `plotB.laz`). |
| `/outside` | | Keep points outside every polygon instead of inside. |

: Options used in the `clipdata` examples. {#tbl-options-clipdata}

## Outputs

One LAS or LAZ file per run, or with `/multifile` one file per polygon
(`<field value>.laz`), each with the input's point format and coordinate
system.

## Results

@fig-clipdata-maps shows the clips from above. On the left, the box and
plot points fill their black outlines exactly. On the right, the
outside-plots clip covers the tile except for two empty circles that
match the plot outlines. @fig-clipdata-height shows the height-limited
clip from the side, in height above ground: every kept point (blue) sits
above the dashed 2 ft line, and the grey points below it were in the box
but too low.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/clipdata_figures.md >}}

## Checks

@tbl-checks-clipdata compares each clip with the same clip made in R. The
box clip must match exactly. The per-plot and outside-plot clips must be
within 0.5%, because a point lying exactly on a plot boundary can
legitimately fall on either side. The height-limited clip is checked
point by point against the 2-200 ft limits.
